output.name: Keret
output.myth: Keret is the tern who flies from pole to pole and back each year. Hesk counts the birds at the pole and says one is missing. Tavo the Gale pushed Keret off course in autumn, and the people grieved at the cliff, burned a little smoke, and mended her nets for no one. Then, in the dead of winter, a wet shape comes over the headland. She lands on the wrong stake, shakes salt over the hearth, and asks whether any fish is left. The Gulls shriek the news across Vel. Nobody had said she was dead, only late. Aun laughed at that, since Aun is always late too. So if you are lost, do not be ashamed to come home wet. Hesk will keep your place on the Spindle, and Keret will tell you where the wind went.
output.verse:
Who came back wet, late?
Keret shook sea from her wings.
Late, and unashamed.
